bug_semantics: Reflected XSS in the embedded MCP HTTP server: the unsanitized mcp query parameter is interpolated into HTML and into a JavaScript string inside getHtmlPage, so a crafted localhost URL executes attacker JS in the MCP origin and can read/write diagram session APIs.
flaw_origin: First write of packages/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts in 79aa8734f15936483a38901c0c359b757578e0a1 (feat: add MCP server package for npx distribution). Parent cd76fa615e928e14fc510b94cb7db94f304cbe57 has no mcp-server tree. The commit reads url.searchParams.get("mcp") and embeds it as const sessionId = "${sessionId}"; plus unescaped HTML. Main-line squash 439bdd4577ff70fe65583a904c18473945c1cf8e (#284) carries the identical blob and is not the BIC.
ai_marker: none; BIC author/committer Dayuan Jiang <jdy.toh@gmail.com>; no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot author on the commit object
evidence: CVE-2026-73037 is PUBLISHED (VulnCheck CNA; GHSA withdrawn_at null). Issue #917 remains OPEN with the same two sinks. HEAD 155ef4f7acd29c9d46fb6fc35c92e6e6955a6ce1 still has searchParams.get("mcp") at http-server.ts:264, HTML ${sessionId.slice(-8)} at :638, and const sessionId = "${sessionId}"; at :700. git cat-file -e parent:packages/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts fails (path absent). git log -1 authors on 79aa873 are human. CORS/bind later commits (67b0d77, 41c410c) do not encode the mcp interpolations. Maintainer closed earlier #755 as won't-fix (localhost/click-required). No XSS-encoding commit on origin/main.
reasoning: Real CWE-79 reflected XSS: attacker-controlled ?mcp= is written unescaped into HTML and a JS string. Vulnerability-first BIC is the first-write of those lines (79aa873), not the later #284 squash. BIC commit object is human-authored with no AI markers, so NOT_AI. potential_fix.approach: Validate session IDs to a conservative charset before render; insert into JS via JSON.stringify(sessionId); HTML-encode any display slice; keep CORS same-origin.
potential_fix.rationale: JSON.stringify closes the JS-string breakout (" ; //); HTML encoding closes markup injection; charset validation removes a render-time bypass even if a later template forgets to escape.
